```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
# Bash chunks are a record of commands you ran in the Terminal. Knitting shows
# them but doesn't run them again.
knitr::opts_hooks$set(engine = function(options) {
  if (options$engine == "bash") options$eval <- FALSE
  options
})
```

<!--
Explain what this step does and why, and copy each command you ran into a
bash chunk. R chunks run from the top of the repository.
-->
```{steps: bin_quality}

# 1. Move to [checkm] file directory
```{bash}
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/checkm

# 2. Find the longest contig within the bins using the following command:
```{bash}
cat ../flye/bbd/assembly.fasta | bioawk -c fastx '{print length($seq),$name}' | sort -n

# 3. Replace the template code below (contig_XX) with the longest contig number:
```{bash}
samtools faidx ../flye/bbd/assembly.fasta contig_XX > ../metabat/bins_bbd/contig_XX.fa
cp ../metabat/bins_bbd/*.fa bins_bbd/

# 4. Run a slurm script for checkm in a text file <run_checkm_bbd.sh>
```

```{steps: bin_selection}

# 1. Change directory to [checkm] (again)
```{bash}
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/checkm

# 2. View results from [checkm_results_bbd.txt] using <head>, <cat>, <more> or <less>
```{bash}
head checkm_results_bbd.txt
head -n 20 checkm_results_bbd.txt

## Focus on bins with a completeness greater than 15%
cat checkm_results_bbd.txt | awk '$13>15'

## We just want the ID of the bin, so use the following script instead:
cat checkm_results_bbd.txt | awk '$13>15{print $1}'

## Send the output to a file to use in the next step:
cat checkm_results_bbd.txt | awk '$13>15{print $1}' > bbd_topbins.txt
```

Completeness and contamination of each bin, estimated with CheckM, and selection of the most complete bins for further analysis. Commands for this step were run in `checkm/`.
